+title: Move idioms-swift to the toolchain swift format
+---
+## What
+
+`builtin/validators/code-hygiene/rules/idioms-swift.md` runs `swiftformat`, the tool of Nick Lockwood. Only Homebrew installs that tool. The new policy is the Swift toolchain and its own `swift format`. Change this rule to run `swift format lint`.
+
+Files to change:
+- `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/rules/idioms-swift.md` — the frontmatter script, the doctor block and the body
+- `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/fixtures/idioms-swift.fail.swift.tmpl`
+- `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/fixtures/idioms-swift.pass.swift.tmpl`
+- `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/tool_rules/tests/shipped/idioms_swift.rs`
+- `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/builtin/mod.rs`
+
+The new script must do this:
+- Write a temporary `.swift-format` configuration file. Make ON only the rules that decide an idiom. Make OFF every rule that decides layout. Review is read-only, thus a layout finding is not correct.
+- Run `swift format lint --strict` one time for each file. Keep the one-run-for-each-file shape. A path that refuses must cost only its own file.
+- Read each output line. A line has this shape: `<file>:<line>:<col>: error: [<RuleName>] <message>`. Write one JSON finding for each line, in the same shape the rule writes today.
+
+Measured on the Swift 6.4 toolchain, these rules decide the idiom bullets:
+
+| the rule | the bullet it decides |
+|---|---|
+| `AlwaysUseLiteralForEmptyCollectionInit` | `idioms.md` empty-collection variables — and in the correct direction |
+| `NoVoidReturnOnFunctionSignature` | `idioms.md` omit the `Void` return clause — BOTH halves |
+| `UseWhereClausesInForLoops` | `idioms.md` a loop that filters says `where` |
+| `DontRepeatTypeInStaticProperties` | `idioms.md` type-name repetition in a static member |
+| `ReplaceForEachWithForLoop` | the `forEach` half of the loop bullet |
+| `UseLetInEveryBoundCaseVariable` | the pattern-let bullet |
+| `UseShorthandTypeNames` | the shorthand type sugar bullet |
+| `UseSynthesizedInitializer` | the redundant memberwise initializer bullet |
+
+`AlwaysUseLiteralForEmptyCollectionInit` and `UseWhereClausesInForLoops` are OFF in the default configuration. The written configuration must make them ON.
+
+Do NOT make ON `NeverForceUnwrap`, `NeverUseForceTry` or `NeverUseImplicitlyUnwrappedOptionals`. `disallowed-constructs-swift` owns those three bullets, and swiftlint keeps the test-target split and the `ignored_literal_argument_functions` option that `swift format` does not have. One requirement takes one owner.
+
+Measure these two facts first, then write them into the rule body:
+- Which Swift version first gives `AlwaysUseLiteralForEmptyCollectionInit` and `UseWhereClausesInForLoops`. That version is the new floor, in place of the `--min-version 0.62.1` floor.
+- If `UseWhereClausesInForLoops` reports `things.filter { $0 > 2 }.forEach { thing in print(thing) }`. `idioms.md` names that shape as its second DON'T.
+
+The gate loses 22 rules that the toolchain does not have: the performance group, the Swift Testing group, the SwiftUI group, `preferFinalClasses`, `redundantEquatable`, `genericExtensions`, `opaqueGenericParameters`, `ifExpressions` and `conditionalAssignment`. Two of those decided a prompt bullet. The task "Prompt rules take back the bullets the toolchain gate loses" gives those two bullets back to the prompt rules. Do not delete them here without that task.
+
+The script becomes much smaller. Remove the `--rules` intersection with `swiftformat --rules`, the `--min-version` test, and the four command-line options. The toolchain gives a fixed set of 43 rules, and each rule is only ON or OFF.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] The script names `swift format` and names `swiftformat` nowhere.
+- [ ] `doctor.check_command` tests the toolchain. `doctor.fix_hint` names the toolchain, because Homebrew does not install it.
+- [ ] A Swift file that has only wrong indentation gives 0 findings.
+- [ ] The failing fixture gives one finding for each rule the configuration makes ON, at exit 0.
+- [ ] The passing fixture gives 0 findings, exit 0 and 0 bytes on stderr.
+- [ ] A path that holds no file costs only its own file, and writes one `sah-diagnostic:` line.
+- [ ] The rule body records the new Swift version floor and both measurements above.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Update every test in `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/tool_rules/tests/shipped/idioms_swift.rs`. Delete the tests that hold the swiftformat roster and the 0.62.1 floor. Write a test that holds the new rule roster to standing in `swift format dump-configuration`.
+- [ ] Write a test that holds the gate to reporting the DO of the empty-collection bullet no longer, and to reporting the DON'T. This replaces `the_shipped_swift_idioms_tool_rule_decides_no_empty_collection_declaration`, because the toolchain now decides that bullet in the correct direction.
+- [ ] Write a test that holds the gate silent on a file that has only layout defects.
+- [ ] Update the bullet-ownership tests in `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/builtin/mod.rs` for the bullets the toolchain takes and for the bullets it gives back.
+- [ ] Run `cargo test -p swissarmyhammer-validators swift`. Every test passes.
+- [ ] Run `sah doctor`. The rule reports as healthy, and its fixture pair passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write the failing tests first, then write the code that makes them pass. #swift
